All three collinearity diagnostics on a fitted model

Source: R/collinearity.R
mm_collinearity_report.Rd

Runs mm_vif_check() on the fit and mm_redun_check() and mm_cor_pairs() on the development predictors, and reports them together.

Usage

mm_collinearity_report(model, cohort, max_vif = 4, max_r2 = 0.9, max_rho = 0.5)

Arguments

model

An mm_model().

cohort

The rows the model was developed on.

max_vif, max_r2, max_rho

Passed to the three checks above.

Value

A list with vif, redun, pairs, ok (the VIF and redundancy checks; the pair matrix is advisory and does not gate), and text.

Details

The cohort is required and is checked against the model's development fingerprint, because mm_model() does not retain the rows it was fitted on. Collinearity measured on a different frame of the same shape would describe a different sample and read as though it described the fit.

The outcome column is removed before the redundancy and correlation checks: a predictor correlated with the OUTCOME is the point of the model, not a problem with it.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 250, seed = 5)
fit <- suppressWarnings(mm_model(
  mm_project("collin", "event", c("age", "bmi"), cohort = cohort), cohort))
cat(mm_collinearity_report(fit, cohort)$text)
#> VIF: per variable: highest 1.00 (age, 1 df), none at or above 4; per parameter: highest 1.00 (age), none at or above 4
#>   redundancy: none at R2 >= 0.9; highest is age at 0.000
#>   pairs: no numeric pair at |rho| >= 0.5
